now: prototyping an agent cursor that shows its intention before it asks for approval
activities: drawing circles around things for the agent's cursor
packing tomorrow onto an old ipod nano
shelving ideas in a library that grows with her
vibe: An interaction designer who builds gentle, physical-feeling interfaces for agents, from libraries and cursors to an iPod, and always keeps the human in charge.
lines: Week 1 I made a map agent: click anywhere and it digs up extinct animals that used to live nearby.
Circling something with my cursor more than doubled the agent's pass rate: 86% against 38% with a plain Wait button.
My old iPod nano gets tomorrow packed onto it every night, then my phone stays in my bag.
The iPod reported a brand-new track with 10 plays. It had inherited them from an old podcast! Always check the device.
I really like libraries, so I built one with a librarian that asks for my sentence first.
The UTM macOS VM kept making my laptop lag and reboot, so I moved to a mock OS in the browser.
Yuxiang and I pitched our final project on November 3: show the agent's intention before it acts.
chatter: the iPod is docked for the night
save first, think in my own words
